note: EXAMPLE ONLY, published to show the format. A real private run config, and the plugins that define its held-out domains and genres, must NOT be published or committed to a public repository before the evaluation: anyone who sees them can tune a model to the held-out sets. Keep them private and draw a fresh random nonce for every config (python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(16))"). Give every plugin with the SHA-256 of its bytes, as {"path": "plugins/tides.py", "sha256": "<sha256sum plugins/tides.py>"}: the config names a plugin by its path, so only the SHA-256 makes the commitment cover what the held-out domain or genre is, and evalgen refuses to run a plugin whose bytes differ from it. What the evaluator publishes: before the evaluation, only the two commitments that cli.py generate records in the run's manifest (seed_commitment and private_config_commitment), never the manifest itself, which holds the seed; after the evaluation, this config, its plugin files and the seed with its nonce. Anyone can then check the config against the commitment published before the evaluation with python cli.py verify-config --commitment HEX CONFIG, with HEX that published value (verify-config RUN_DIR CONFIG only says that a config and a run agree: a run regenerated from a swapped config agrees with it), and regenerating the run checks every plugin against its SHA-256. Regenerating executes the plugins' code, in-process and with your rights: the SHA-256 pins which code runs, not that it is safe, so read the plugins first or regenerate in a sandbox (verify-config runs none). The SHA-256 covers a plugin's own bytes only, so a plugin must be self-contained: no reads of other files, the environment, the clock or the network, and imports from evalgen and the standard library only. Plugin paths are relative to this file. This example holds out the test-only toy domain and toy genre of tests/, which are public and hide nothing from anyone, so it names them by path alone (a checkout may change their line endings, and so their bytes): use it to demo the held-out metrics offline, e.g. python cli.py demo --mix random --private-config configs/private.example.json
